title.value: Mutations associated with neuropsychiatric conditions delineate functional brain connectivity dimensions contributing to autism and schizophrenia
title.justification: The title is directly derived from the research article, which focuses on analyzing the impact of mutations on brain connectivity and their contribution to autism and schizophrenia.
title.quote: Mutations associated with neuropsychiatric conditions delineate functional brain connectivity dimensions contributing to autism and schizophrenia

analysis.description: The study examines how specific mutations, particularly 16p11.2 and 22q11.2 CNVs, affect functional brain connectivity and contribute to autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and schizophrenia (SZ). It analyzes connectivity using resting-state fMRI data and explores the shared connectivity signatures across idiopathic and genetic conditions.

type.justification: The paper involves the practical analysis of resting-state brain connectivity data from a significant number of individuals to understand the impact of CNVs on neuropsychiatric conditions.
type.quote: Here we report an analysis of resting-state FC using magnetic resonance imaging data from 101 CNV carriers, 755 individuals with idiopathic ASD, SZ, or ADHD and 1,072 controls.

name.justification: The study primarily investigates how genetic variations influence brain connectivity, particularly in neuropsychiatric conditions such as autism and schizophrenia. This situates it within the domain of neuroscience.
name.quote: CNVs have large mirror effects on FC at the global and regional level.

name.justification: The study applies neuroimaging techniques like fMRI to clinical populations to understand pathological conditions, which is a key aspect of clinical neuroscience.
name.quote: Functional connectivity (FC) represents the intrinsic low-frequency synchronization between different neuroanatomical regions.

name.justification: The research addresses psychiatric conditions such as autism spectrum disorder and schizophrenia, making it relevant to the field of psychiatry.
name.quote: ADHD, ASD, and SZ are discussed as part of the analysis in connection with connectome signatures.

name.justification: The dataset includes data related to genetic variations and their impact on individuals and is extensively used in the study.
name.quote: 16p11.2 deletion and duplication carriers (29.6–30.1 MB; Hg19), and extrafamilial controls from the Simons Variation in Individuals Project (VIP) consortium.
